newsitem.title: UK: Redland shares up on results, disposal plan.
newsitem.headline: Redland shares up on results, disposal plan.

text.p: Shares in Redland Plc climbed on Thursday as the building materials group posted profits in line with expectations and said it was in talks to sell its French aggregates business, dealers said.
The shares rose 18p to 371-1/2 by 0953 GMT.
"The French operations were always something of a problem and it's positive news that they're getting rid of them," one market-maker said. "That's been the real good news today."
Redland's pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits fell to 259.1 million stg in 1996 from 273.2 million the previous year. Analysts' forecasts ranged from 212 million stg to 308 million
The dividend was held at 16.67p, as expected
Chief executive Robert Napier told Reuters that Redland was in talks with "a number of interested parties" to sell its French aggregates business.

"The results were slightly better than some had expected and they have already made so many profit warnings that it's positive that they are out of the way," one dealer said. "The dividend was maintained, and there's a chance the company could be a takeover target, so the stock should rally."
